# `silk/time/period`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Calendar spans: the [`Period`](#Period) type, a number of years, months, weeks, and days with an exact
time part, as in "1 month and 2 days".

## When to use

Use [`Period`](#Period) for a span that a person counts on a calendar: a monthly bill, an age, three
weeks of leave. Its length in seconds depends on where it starts, because months and years
differ in length and a day in a time zone can have 23 or 25 hours. For a span of a fixed
length, such as a timeout, use `Duration` of `silk.time.duration`.

## Details

A `Period` has four calendar fields and one `Duration` for the time below a day. All parts
that are not zero have the same sign. The calendar fields are not balanced: 14 months stay
14 months, and 1 month is not equal to 30 days. The time part is exact, so 90 minutes and
1 hour 30 minutes are the same value.

The text form is the ISO 8601 duration, such as `P1Y2M3DT4H30M`. `PlainDate.addPeriod` and
`PlainDate.periodUntil` of `silk.time.plain_date`, and the same functions of
`silk.time.plain_date_time`, apply a period to a date and measure one. `RelativeTo` of
`silk.time.relative` rounds a period, counts it in one unit, and changes its largest unit,
from a starting point.

## Examples

### Read a period and look at its parts

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.period { Period }
import silk.time.text { TimeParseError }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  match Period.parse("P1Y2M10DT2H30M") {
    Result<Period, TimeParseError>.Success { value } => {
      if value.years() != 1 || value.months() != 2 || value.weeks() != 0 || value.days() != 10 {
        return 1
      }
      if value.time().wholeSeconds() != 9000 {
        return 2
      }
      if value.negate().sign() != -1 {
        return 3
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<Period, TimeParseError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 4
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="DateUnit"></a>

## `DateUnit`

```silk
pub enum DateUnit
```

The largest calendar unit of a measured [`Period`](#Period).

### Details

`PlainDate.periodUntil` counts in this unit first and in the smaller units after it. With
`Month`, the span from January 1 of one year to March 1 of the next is 14 months; with
`Year`, it is 1 year and 2 months; with `Day`, it is 424 or 425 days.

<a id="Period"></a>

## `Period`

```silk
pub struct Period
```

A calendar span: years, months, weeks, days, and an exact time part.

### Details

All parts that are not zero have the same sign. `==` and `!=` compare part by part, so
`P1M` and `P30D` are not equal, and neither are `P7D` and `P1W`.

`Display` writes an ISO 8601 duration, such as `P1Y2M3DT4H30M`, `-P3W`, or `PT0S` for the
empty period.

<a id="Period.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(years: i64, months: i64, weeks: i64, days: i64, time: Duration) -> Period
```

Returns the period with the given parts.

#### Gotchas

Parts with different signs, or a part outside the range, trap. [`Period.checkedMake`](#Period.impl.checkedMake)
returns `None` instead.

<a id="Period.impl.checkedMake"></a>

### Associated function `checkedMake`

```silk
pub fn checkedMake(years: i64, months: i64, weeks: i64, days: i64, time: Duration) -> Option<Period>
```

Returns the period with the given parts, or `None` when two parts have different signs or
a part is outside the range.

#### Details

Years, months, and weeks are at most 4,294,967,295 in each direction. The days, as 24
hours each, and the time part are together less than 2^53 seconds. These are the limits of
ECMAScript Temporal.

<a id="Period.impl.checkedAdd"></a>

### Method `checkedAdd`

```silk
pub fn checkedAdd(self: Self, other: Period) -> Option<Period>
```

Returns the sum of this period and `other`, part by part, or `None` when the parts of the
sum have different signs or a part is outside the range.

#### Details

Nothing is balanced: `P1M` plus `P20D` is `P1M20D`. `P1M` plus `-P1D` has no result,
because the length of the sum depends on the month.

<a id="Period.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<Period, TimeParseError>
```

Reads a period from an ISO 8601 duration such as `P1Y2M3DT4H30M`.

#### Details

The text is an optional sign, `P`, and then counts with the designators `Y`, `M`, `W`, and
`D`, then `T` and counts with `H`, `M`, and `S`, in that order. Each part can be absent,
but at least one is present. The last time count can have a fraction of one to nine digits
after `.` or `,`, as in `PT1.5H` or `PT0.25S`. Letter case does not matter. A leading `-`
makes every part negative.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that
  form.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if the parts are outside the range of
  [`Period.checkedMake`](#Period.impl.checkedMake).
